thread:
Aria: Heads up — I hit a type inference mismatch between our ESM and CJS bundles while onboarding an edge app. ESM picks the primitive overload, CJS picks the generic and T lands as any.

Ben: do you have the overloads handy?

Aria: simplified:
function makeClient<T extends object>(opts: { auth: T }): Client<T>
function makeClient(opts: { auth: string }): Client<{ token: string }>
Callsite: makeClient({ auth: process.env.SDK_KEY }) — ESM infers token overload, CJS picks generic -> T = any.

Priya: That screams moduleResolution/interop shape. Are we emitting different .d.ts or using export default vs module.exports?

Aria: We ship both entries; the .cjs wrapper uses module.exports. Consumers with esModuleInterop see different shapes.

Ben: quick fixes: (1) reorder overloads so primitive/string comes first, (2) add a narrow string overload before the generic, (3) add a tiny discriminant like authKind?: 'token' on the primitive overload to avoid ambiguity.

Priya: Also document recommended tsconfig for edge: module: ESNext or moduleResolution: nodeNext, and call out that older moduleResolution: node can change conditional type resolution.

Aria: I'll open a PR with overload reorder + example in examples/edge-tsconfig showing tsconfig snippets and a note about unknown vs any. Will also add a unit-types test asserting the inferred Client<{ token: string }> for the env string case.

devx-bot: PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/501 created. CI: typings-check queued. :eyes:

Ben: Nice. If we still see support churn we can add a quick runtime check in the Console that warns when a package uses the CJS interop pattern. Low friction.

Priya: Also consider making the generic overload require an explicit type param in ambiguous cases so inference can't default to any.

Aria: Good idea. I'll prototype both changes in the PR and include a short snippet in the onboarding guide for edge consumers. Thanks everyone!
